previous_statement: The local fixed-point index depends only on the pointed map germ and is invariant under a coordinate identification: it is computed after restricting to any sufficiently small isolating neighbourhood. The chart kappa identifies the germ of G at p with the germ of T(y)=Ay at 0, and node 1.3.1 shows that 0 is isolated for T. Therefore ind(G,p)=J(T,0)=J(A,0). Combining with the preceding step yields J(A,0)=sgn det(I-A).
new_statement: Discard the compact-extension comparison. For T(y)=Ay and h:=id-T=I-A, the defining relation for the local fixed-point index at the isolated fixed point 0 is J(A,0):=J(T,0)=d(h,V) on any sufficiently small isolating ball V. Node 1.3.2 computes this Brouwer degree as d(h,V)=sgn det(I-A). Hence J(A,0)=sgn det(I-A); no germ invariance, coordinate invariance, or invocation of node 1.3.1 is required.
